title: Senior asks: write() decides 201 or 200 with file_exists() BEFORE it saves. Two users create new.json at the same moment. What can happen?
options: Both get 201, but only one file exists
One request gets a 500 from PHP
explain: Both check file_exists() while the file is missing, so both say 'new' and return 201. The last write wins. The check and the save are not one atomic step. A safe way is fopen($path, 'x') for create, like FileNameResolver does.

title: Senior asks: the controller does strtolower() on the action. A client sends DELETE /?action=DELETE&file=a.csv. What happens?
explain: strtolower('DELETE') gives 'delete', which is in ACTION_METHODS and expects the DELETE method. So the request works. It is friendly, but also two spellings for one thing. Decide on one rule and test it.

title: Senior asks: you want to make FileService final. FileControllerTest uses createMock(FileService::class). What happens?
options: PHPUnit fails: a final class cannot be doubled
The test passes but is slower
explain: PHPUnit builds a mock as a subclass. A final class cannot be extended, so createMock() throws. Fix: give FileService an interface (FileServiceInterface), type the controller against it, and mock the interface.

title: Senior asks: write() saves each row with fputcsv($out, $row). Row 2 has the keys in another order. What does this print?
explain: A CSV line has no names, only positions. fputcsv() writes the values in the order of the array. Row 2 starts with fruit, so 'pear' lands under the id column. Re-order every row by the header keys before writing.

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: 10 <=> 9 compares two ints: 1. In PHP 8 a number and a NON-numeric string are compared as strings: '10' vs '9a', and '1' < '9', so the result is -1. In PHP 7 this was a number compare. Always cast before you sort.

title: What does Node print?
explain: sort() without a function compares the values as strings. '10' comes before '9' because '1' < '9'. For numbers use sort((a, b) => a - b).

title: PHP 8. B extends A. What does this print?
explain: new static creates the class that was called (late static binding): B::s() gives B. new self is fixed to the class where the code is written: A. Use static for factories that child classes may extend.

title: You ran git add config.php by mistake. You want to unstage it but keep your edits. Which command?
explain: git restore --staged takes the file out of the index, the working file stays as it is. git restore config.php (no flag) would throw your edits away. reset --hard drops everything. Check with git status first.
